verifiedAgainst.note: Verified: project-scoped MCP servers live in a `.mcp.json` at the project root, checked into version control, in the standardized shape {"mcpServers": {"<name>": {...}}}. A stdio server carries command/args/env; an http server carries type and url. THE FILE FORMAT IS VERIFIED; THE CONTENT MODEL IS NOT VENDOR-SPECIFIED. docs/SPEC.md section 10.9 asks for 'an MCP server manifest' without saying what a document-derived one should contain, so what this target puts inside the verified envelope is our design and is described in vendorFields.

vendorFields.contentModel: One server entry. Its command and args are template scaffolding, declared here and therefore exempt from the traceability gate exactly as a Markdown heading is. Its `env` block is the only unit-derived part: one key per environmentVariable unit, each traceable to the unit and through it to a source locator. Nothing in this file is prose, so the gate runs over derived key/value pairs rather than over segmented sentences.
vendorFields.honestyNote: The server this manifest scaffolds is the stdio MCP server inside @markforge/cli, exposing convert, fmt, and agentify. Re-derived 2026-08-01 under the B+ publishing decision (docs/decisions/PUBLISHING.md): `npx -y @markforge/cli mcp` needs no global install, which is what an MCP client configuration on a clean machine actually has, and the unscoped name it would otherwise use belongs to somebody else's package. It previously scaffolded the bare `markforge mcp` binary, correct only for a user who had already installed it globally. This field earns its length because it has been wrong about its own profile twice. First it claimed the manifest named `markforge serve` while the scaffold said `npx -y @markforge/mcp` — a different command, and `markforge serve` is the HTTP API, which would hang if an MCP client spawned it on stdio. Then `@markforge/mcp` named a package nothing published; under B+ that package stays private and the CLI is what publishes, so the scope in this command changed for a reason rather than for tidiness. The dropped `--context .markforge/provenance.json` argument was a flag no server ever accepted. STATUS.md and docs/TARGETS.md both repeated the `markforge serve` claim, inheriting the error from here, which is why scripts/check-target-docs.mjs now validates this field against the scaffold beside it.
